reported.title: Short press below settle time never triggers buzzer
reported.description: The debounce in scanButton() only accepts a level once it has been stable for SETTLE_MS=15 ms (lines 27-32), so a press shorter than that never reaches the `down && !held` branch at line 35 and acknowledge() is never called. The measured evidence confirms this: "D11 missed 1 of 1 trigger(s): D11 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 2.00 s" in the "very short press below settle" scenario. D11 missed 1 of 1 trigger(s): D11 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 2.00 s.

reported.title: Blocking delay() in acknowledge() stalls the heartbeat
reported.description: acknowledge() calls delay(BUZZ_MS) for 300 ms (line 19), which blocks loop() so the heartbeat check at line 63 cannot run on schedule, and lastBeat is then reset to the late millis() at line 65, accumulating phase error. The measured evidence shows gaps of 699-798 ms against the 500±120 ms requirement, e.g. "gap of 798 ms" and "first line only at 724 ms". Expected /^alive [0-9]+$/ every 500 ± 120 ms; 5 of 13 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 798 ms.

truth.description: The acknowledgement waits 300 ms inside delay(), so a heartbeat that falls due during it is printed up to 300 ms late; only presses that land shortly before a heartbeat show it

truth_for_judge.description: The acknowledgement waits 300 ms inside delay(), so a heartbeat that falls due during it is printed up to 300 ms late; only presses that land shortly before a heartbeat show it

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial lines matching '^alive \\d+$' every 500 ms (Heartbeat every 500 ms)

judge_input.spec:
- Call button on D5 with internal pull-up (active LOW); buzzer on D11.
- A settled press on D5 sounds the buzzer: D11 HIGH for 300 ms, starting within 100 ms of the press.
- Contact bounce up to 10 ms on press and release must not sound the buzzer twice.
- Presses while the buzzer is sounding are ignored.
- D11 stays LOW whenever no press has been accepted.
- Print `alive <n>` every 500 ms ±120 ms, with n counting the lines printed.
